newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ housing costs main contributor to CPI rise.
newsitem.headline: NZ housing costs main contributor to CPI rise.

text.p: The Consumer Price Index rose by 0.7 percent in the December 1996 quarter for a 2.6 percent rise in the December year, Statistics New Zealand said on Friday.
This followed rises of 0.6 percent in the September quarter and 0.8 percent in the June quarter.
"Housing costs contributed the most to the rise in the CPI, recording a rise of 0.7 percent. This was mostly due to a rise in local authority rates and in house and flat rentals," SNZ said.
"Nearly every group in the CPI is showing a similar sort of increase, so there really is a firming up in that sort of level of inflation," government statistician Len Cook told reporters.
"Housing now is growing, in fact, marginally less than the rate of inflation overall. That's good news," he said.
Personal and health care rose 1.7 percent largely due to a rise in the cost of medical insurance.
In transportation, international and domestic airfares rose, as did the cost of vehicle insurance. Petrol prices also rose, but the prices of used and new cars fell again in the December quarter.
Credit services recorded a rise of 0.9 percent. Hire purchase charges on furniture and appliances contributed most to the increase.
Household operation costs rose 0.5 percent due to the prices of plants increasing, along with the prices of crockery and dinnerware and electricity. Telephone call charges fell.

Overall tobacco and alcohol prices rose 0.6 percent in December. Price rises were recorded for beer consumed on licensed premises, cigarettes and spirits. The price of beer consumed off licensed premises fell.
Apparel costs rose 0.7 percent, driven by rises in the cost of clothing fabrics and children's footwear. The prices of children's casual sports shoes and women's knitwear fell.

A fall in the cost of home computers and software, and cinema, theatre and concert tickets, contributed to the overall fall of 0.2 percent in recreation and education in December. Counter-acting these were rises in the cost of fitness and recreation activities, and hotel and motel accommodation.
Excluding credit services, the CPI rose by 0.7 percent this quarter. Since the December 1995 quarter this index has increased by 2.4 percent.
The Superannuitants Price Index for All Households rose by 0.9 percent for the quarter, and by 2.7 percent since December 1995, SNZ said.
